solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person trying to nab another's second drink

definitions.meaning: someone in pursuit, trying to catch the person ahead
a drink taken straight after another, such as a beer after a whisky

explanation.surface: A pursuer grabs somebody else's follow-up drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a pursuer, and a follow-up drink swallowed after a first one.

clue.text: Special period in which there's no integrity

indicators.note: the period word holds the next word within it

parts.note: an hour can be a particular special time, as in 'our finest hour'

explanation.surface: A special era when nobody can be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which there's' signals the insertion; 'Special period' reads as an era, but means a particular hour of note, as in 'finest hour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrity and this word are synonyms for upright moral principle.

clue.text: Gift claimed by Sibyl back on location, we hear

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it, i.e. support it

indicators.note: signals that the word for location is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A prophetess claims a gift, supported by being in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns SITE into its sound-alike SIGHT. A Sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyance, the supposed power of seeing the future, is the gift a prophetess would claim.

clue.text: 1 across, say, or 1 across drunk by English

indicators.note: being drunk leaves the letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, the word for a pursuer or a follow-up drink

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a follow-up drink consumed by an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives the anagram RACEHORS. 'say' marks the definition as an example: a steeplechaser is one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser, which races over fences, is an example of a horse bred and trained for racing.

clue.text: On-field evidence of underground move to purge players?

parts.note: to worm an animal is to purge it of parasitic worms
the cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: A sports report on a manager purging the squad, seen on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move to purge players' reads like a football club clearing out its squad; 'to purge' is the verb for dosing an animal against parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: The coiled heap of soil a burrowing earthworm leaves on a lawn or pitch shows where it moved below.

clue.text: Win over the French added to women's respect

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to heed is to pay respect or attention to
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Winning people round by adding French courtesy to respect for women.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with flattery is a way to persuade them, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Repetitive movement from knocker on door

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: The repeated motion of a door knocker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of knockeR ON DOor.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music whose main theme keeps returning is a classical form often used as a final movement.

clue.text: Transport info for citizens provided here

definitions.meaning: a taxi is a means of transport
the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British charity giving free advice to the public, is abbreviated this way

explanation.surface: A transport information point for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citizens Advice Bureau is a UK charity that gives free legal and money advice; its initials are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired vehicle, and the letters also stand for the British advice charity's bureau.

clue.text: Sailor abroad set aside

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
away from home, overseas

explanation.surface: A sailor overseas puts something by.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something for later is to save it, a phrasal verb synonym of reserve.

clue.text: Means of transport connected works with college

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a cycle is a set of linked works, such as a song cycle

explanation.surface: A transport link joining the works site to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-wheeled pedalled vehicle is a way of getting around, so it is a means of transport.

clue.text: It's said writer will express tentative interest

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: a nib is a writing point; nib'll is a contraction of 'nib will'

explanation.surface: Reportedly a writer will show cautious interest in an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' asks for the sound of NIB'LL (nib will).
explanation.definitionFit: To take small bites at an offer is an idiom for showing cautious interest without committing.

clue.text: Monarch's heartless companion put out

indicators.note: one of the central letters of the royal word is removed

parts.note: a queen is a monarch; the 's here is 'has'
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A queen's cruel consort is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops one middle E of QUEEN, leaving QUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To extinguish a fire is to put it out, a synonym.

clue.text: Bishop's said no different church must be included

indicators.note: the church letters are placed within the rearranged letters
the letters of these two words are made different, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The bishop said no, and a different church must be brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns SAID NO into DIOSAN; 'must be included' puts CE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to a diocese, the district a bishop governs.

clue.text: Boost canteen menu briefly with hot stew

indicators.note: the letters are stewed, i.e. mixed together
the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Livening up a canteen menu with a hot stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts MENU to MEN; 'stew' mixes CANTEEN, MEN and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvement or increase is a boost, so the noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Unorthodox setters, each vastly superior

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 'a head' means each, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: Crossword setters with odd methods each rate themselves far better than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodox' rearranges SETTERS into STREETS.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for being far better than the rest, the opposite of trailing behind.

clue.text: Bowlers finally cured, as whole team needs to be?

definitions.text: as whole team needs to be?

indicators.note: the end letter of the cricket word is taken

parts.note: kippered fish is cured by salting and smoking

explanation.surface: A cricket side: the bowlers are at last fixed, as the team must be.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowlers deliver the ball; a team needs a captain, a skipper, to lead it.
explanation.definitionFit: Every side must be captained, so being led by a captain is what a whole team needs.

clue.text: Avoided what host did in pub?

definitions.meaning: a host at the bar bought drinks for everyone

explanation.surface: Someone dodged their turn to buy, unlike the host at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub, people take turns buying 'a round' of drinks for the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means circumvented, and also bought a round of drinks for the company.

clue.text: Worshippers go on creating havoc

indicators.note: creating havoc throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Churchgoers keep causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'havoc' rearranges GO ON CREATING.
explanation.definitionFit: The gathered members of a church at worship are collectively its assembly of faithful.

clue.text: Specialist diplomat cut off offensive ambassador

indicators.note: the final letter of the military word is chopped

parts.note: an offensive is a military attack
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An offensive ambassador cut off a specialist diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' drops the K of ATTACK. HE stands for His or Her Excellency, the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy official with a particular field, such as a military or cultural one, holds this title.

clue.text: Part of pump beginning to swivel stops mine working

indicators.note: the letter stops up, or plugs, the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a mine

indicators.note: only the first letter of the turning word is used

parts.note: on means switched on, working

explanation.surface: A broken swivel part keeps a mine pump from working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' places S inside PIT, giving PIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump draws fluid with a sliding plunger inside a cylinder, one of its working components.

clue.text: Extend series of organs, etc, having expert as leader

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a tract is a connected system of organs, as in the digestive tract

explanation.surface: An organ recital series extended with an expert in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something in time is to extend it, a synonym.

clue.text: Enlivened old king admitted to enormous dread

indicators.note: the two letters are let into the dread word

parts.note: awe is overwhelming fear and wonder
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An aged king was roused by overwhelming fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' puts OK inside AWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused from sleep or stirred into life, the past tense of the verb for coming alive.

clue.text: Quietly judge team returning for initial qualifier

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a ref, referee, judges a match

indicators.note: the team numeral is read backwards

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A referee quietly judges a team coming back for a qualifying round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns XI into IX.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, letters placed at the start of a word to modify its meaning qualify it from the front.

clue.text: Enters the lists with nothing out of place? Exactly

indicators.note: the zero letter is shifted to another spot in the word

parts.note: the lists were the arena for tournaments; a knight entering them jousts
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A knight rides into the tournament with everything precisely in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' moves the O of JOUSTS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning arranged precisely right, as in Kipling's tales, hence exactly.

clue.text: Headgear provided by mum, temperature rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ma is a word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum supplies a hat as the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses MAT, read upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish woollen cap, short for tam-o'-shanter, is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Warship conquistador's docked taking surgeon aboard

indicators.note: the surgeon is put on board, inside the shortened name
the tail letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Cortes was the Spanish conquistador who conquered Mexico; the 's is 'is'
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A Spanish explorer's ship ties up with a surgeon on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the name's last letter, leaving CORTE; 'aboard' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, fast naval escort vessel is a type of fighting ship.

clue.text: Eponymous hero, graduate in a woman's clutches

indicators.note: the outer letters grip the degree letters

parts.note: a dame is a woman; the 's is 'has'
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A hero whose name is a book's title is held tight by a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutches' signals the insertion. 'Eponymous' means the hero gives his name to the work: George Eliot's 1859 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1859 novel takes its title from its central character, a carpenter.

clue.text: Devoted pet welcoming first of travellers home

indicators.note: the pet word takes the letters in

parts.note: a dog is a pet

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the journeying word is used

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A loyal pet greets the first traveller arriving home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' signals the insertion; 'home' gives the two letters for 'at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing fond, excessive affection is being devoted to someone, a synonym.
